## Authoritative Simple Loop mapping

| Koploper block | Bezetmelder (name) | Koploper-internal feedback ID | Logical section | Planned physical amp | Next block |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 1.01 | 101 | 1 | 1 | 2 |
| 2 | 1.02 | 102 | 2 | 3 | 3 |
| 3 | 1.03 | 103 | 3 | 4 | 4 |
| 4 | 1.04 | 104 | 4 | 6 | 1 |

The Simple Loop is a closed 4-block oval with **no switches** and **one bezetmelder per block** (this single-melder rule is specific to the Simple Loop; the general model must keep supporting 0..n melders per block and switch/branch routes).

Locomotives: DCC decoder addresses **1** and **2**; their existing ECoS object IDs are **1000** and **1001**. Stored placement: loc 1 → block 1, loc 2 → block 3.

## Identifier distinctions (do not conflate)

- **Logical section ID** — `LayoutSection.Id` (1..4).
- **Koploper block** — the block number Koploper reports/uses (1..4).
- **Bezetmelder name** — `"1.01"` = module 1, point 1; maps to the C#/ECoS sensor id via `TrackAmplifierOccupancyBridge.TryGetSensorId` (`(module-1)*16 + point`, so `1.01` → sensor 1).
- **Koploper-internal feedback ID** — 101..104 in the JSIF `.dba` records; this is Koploper-internal storage, **not** the ECoS sensor id and **not** the C# bezetmelder representation.
- **DCC decoder address** — 1 / 2. This is what `LocoState.Address` holds and what `IHardwareBackend.SetLocoSpeed(address, ...)` and `IBlockPositionProvider.TryGetBlockForLoc(address)` are keyed by.
- **ECoS object ID** — 1000 / 1001. What Koploper addresses on the ECoS wire; the emulator maps ECoS object ID → decoder address internally.
- **Physical amplifier (ModBus slave)** — 1 / 3 / 4 / 6. A future C# Real binding; Koploper block numbers do **not** express this. Do not infer physical amplifiers from Koploper labels.

## Boundaries

- Koploper describes its own configured blocks/routes/feedback; a graphical `LIJN` drawing does not by itself prove electrical sections or physical amplifier addresses.
- Physical amplifier bindings require their own authoritative source and separate verification (and, later, physical/hardware validation).
- The Python scripts are single-use references for this one JSIF pair, with observed positional field indices and hard-coded `/mnt/data/...` paths. They are suitable as an example transform and test oracle, **not** as a generic tool.
